topics.label: Lecture Introduction
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic opens the lecture, welcomes the students, and outlines the themes of inflammation initiation and resolution.

topics.label: Innate Recognition of Pathogens and Damage via PRR Pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the innate immune system senses infection and cellular damage through molecular patterns, pattern recognition receptors, and downstream signaling complexes.

topics.label: Leukocyte Recruitment, Cell Trafficking, and Systemic Inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how innate activation coordinates the recruitment of circulating immune cells into tissues, their exit via the lymphatic system, and the dangers of systemic inflammatory overactivation.

topics.label: Resolution of Inflammation, Tissue Repair, and Chronic Inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address the mechanisms that terminate acute inflammation, rebuild damaged tissue, and govern chronic inflammatory outcomes such as granuloma formation.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the brief closing remark and indicates the topic for the subsequent lecture.
